prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: rear-end collision in Baytown, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported back strain. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1029; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- Witnesses and the officer say the claimant was not in the vehicle when the crash happened.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: On arrival at the intersection in Baytown, Texas, I found a rear-end collision involving two vehicles. Driver 2 was stopped in the travel lane when the vehicle that Driver 1 had been associated with struck the rear of that car. Driver 1 is named on the policy covering the vehicle involved. Driver 1 later reported back strain, which is a plausible injury for an impact of this kind. The damage to the rear of the struck vehicle is consistent with the force described, and the photographs taken at the scene show the same pattern. Driver 2, a Passenger, and two independent witnesses each described the collision the same way, and their accounts match the physical evidence. Both witnesses and I observed that Driver 1 was not inside the vehicle at the moment of impact. No earlier damage to the vehicle was known to anyone at the scene, and nothing observed suggested a different sequence of events. I have documented the positions of both vehicles, the photographs, and the witness contact details in my supplemental report.
